Passenger Policies
Bluehaven Airways | BHA
Document version 3.0
Effective 2026-07-01 at 00:00:00 UTC
A low-cost airline with optional services priced separately.
1. Scope and definitions
This is a fictional policy publication. All airlines, rules, places, contacts and examples in this document are
invented. It applies only to tickets issued by this airline for flights operated by this airline, including direct and
travel-agency sales. Other carriers, codeshares, group contracts and award tickets are outside its scope.
The document governs requests received on or after its effective date. Except for the issuance-based fee in
Appendix A, these rules apply regardless of original ticket issuance date. Earlier request dates are outside this
publication. A reissue does not change the original ticket issuance timestamp for policy selection.
Flight segment means one scheduled takeoff and landing. An itinerary comprises all segments on one
passenger ticket. A booking may contain several passenger tickets. Travel has started once any segment on
that ticket has been flown. A wholly unused ticket has no flown segments.
Domestic means both endpoints of a segment are in the fictional Republic of Aster; all other segments are
international. Route type is assessed per segment for changes and baggage. For voluntary cancellation, an
itinerary is international if any segment is international; otherwise it is domestic.
1.1 Time and money conventions
All timestamps and elapsed-time calculations use UTC, without daylight-saving adjustments. Departure
proximity is measured from receipt of a complete, authorized request to the scheduled departure time then
recorded on the ticket. For a change, use each affected segment; for cancellation of a wholly unused ticket, use
its first segment. A pending incomplete request does not preserve an earlier deadline.
The early window is 24 hours or more before departure, including exactly 24 hours. The late window is less
than 24 hours but more than 0 hours. At exactly departure time or later, Section 5 applies. All money is USD;
listed fees include any fee-related taxes.

2. Fare types and voluntary changes
Economy Basic, Economy Standard and Economy Flex describe the fare purchased on each ticket. A higher
cabin-baggage allowance or a paid extra does not upgrade a fare. A ticket uses one fare type throughout;
mixed-fare tickets require manual review under Section 9.
2.1 Change fee schedule
The following fees apply per passenger, per changed flight segment, per completed change request.
Multiply by the number of passengers and changed segments. No additional per-booking fee is charged. A new
request after a completed change is charged separately.
Fare Early: at least 24 hours Late: more than 0, less than 24 hours
Economy Basic Not permitted Not permitted
Economy Standard USD 55 current / USD 85 previous Not permitted
Economy Flex USD 15 USD 45
Standard issuance rule: tickets originally issued before 2026-07-01 00:00:00 UTC pay USD 85; those issued at
or after that exact instant pay USD 55. Both apply only in the early window. Appendix A on page 6 preserves the
previous and current rule. The request date or reissue date does not select the fee.
2.2 Fare difference and permitted changes
Every permitted change also requires payment of any positive fare difference for each affected passenger and
segment, even when the change fee is USD 0. Fare difference is the new segment fare minus the old segment
fare, excluding taxes and optional extras. A lower fare creates no refund or credit and cannot offset a change
fee. Changes in unused government taxes are collected or returned to the original payment method separately.
Date or departure-time changes are allowed only where the table permits, subject to seat availability. Airline,
passenger and route endpoint substitutions are not covered by a voluntary change; contact the service desk for
review. You may retain or upgrade the fare type, but not downgrade it. The existing fare determines the change
fee; the replacement fare governs later requests.
2.3 Travel already started
After travel starts, changes to remaining unflown segments follow this table using each segment departure time,
provided no no-show has occurred. A missed segment takes priority over these rules. Voluntary refunds of partly
used tickets are handled only under Section 9.
Example: two Economy Standard travelers on tickets issued on 2026-07-01 change one segment each 30
hours before departure. Fees are 2 x USD 55 = USD 110. With a USD 20 fare increase each, total additional
payment is USD 150, assuming unchanged taxes and no extras.

3. Voluntary cancellation and refunds
This section applies when you choose not to travel and Section 6 does not apply. The table covers cancellation
of the entire wholly unused itinerary for each selected passenger. Cancellation fees are per passenger, per
itinerary, not per segment or per booking.
Fare Early: at least 24 hours Late: more than 0, less than 24 hours
Economy Basic No fare refund or credit No fare refund or credit
Economy Standard No fare refund or credit No fare refund or credit
Economy Flex Travel credit less USD 30 No fare refund or credit
3.1 Amount and payment destination
Fare means the ticket amount excluding separately itemized government taxes and optional services. Where the
table allows a refund or credit, subtract the stated fee from the eligible fare; the result cannot be below USD 0.
No additional balance is collected when the fee exceeds the fare. Unused government taxes are returned to the
original payment method on request for every fare, including non-refundable fares and no-shows.
An original-payment refund returns to the payment instrument used for the original purchase. Paying for another
traveler does not make the fare transferable. A travel credit is issued in the named passenger's name, cannot be
transferred or exchanged for cash, and may be used only with this airline. Unused credit remains available until
expiry.
3.2 Credit validity and optional services
A credit expires exactly 365 elapsed days after issue. It must be redeemed before that instant; redemption at the
expiry instant is not permitted. The new travel must also begin before that expiry instant. There is no extension
under the standard policy.
Purchased baggage and seat extras are non-refundable for a voluntary cancellation. On an eligible date/time
change, unused extras transfer to the same passenger and route without a transfer fee, subject to availability;
unavailable services require manual review. No automatic cash refund is promised for unavailable extras.
4. Cancellation scope
One traveler may cancel their own whole ticket without cancelling other travelers in the booking, after authority is
verified. A request to cancel selected segments only, or any refund after a segment has been flown, requires
Section 9 review; do not apply the whole-ticket table to an assumed remaining balance.
5. No-shows
A traveler is a no-show if no complete authorized change/cancellation request was received before departure
and the traveler does not take that flight. At exactly departure time, a new voluntary request is too late and
receives no-show treatment. All remaining segments are suspended pending service-desk contact; there is no
automatic reinstatement. The remaining fare has no standard refund or credit, including Flex. Unused
government taxes remain refundable. A qualifying airline disruption under Section 6 takes precedence; medical
circumstances may be reviewed under Section 9.

For a wholly unused affected itinerary, refund its full fare, unused government taxes and all unused purchased extras to the original payment method. No cancellation fee, including Economy Basic.
Manual review of the unflown portion and unused extras. The right to refund the unused affected portion remains; the amount and allocation require review. No refund is promised for flown segments.

6. Airline-initiated disruptions
These protections apply when the airline cancels a segment or makes a qualifying schedule change. They
override the voluntary fare restrictions, change fees and no-show loss of value in Sections 2, 3 and 5 for the
affected journey. A passenger choosing to cancel for personal reasons without a qualifying event remains
subject to the voluntary rules.
6.1 Qualifying events
A cancellation by Bluehaven Airways qualifies for all fare types. A schedule change qualifies when the absolute
difference between the original and revised scheduled departure time of a segment is 180 minutes or more,
including exactly 180 minutes, whether moved earlier or later. Smaller changes do not qualify under this
document. Compare the latest notice with the schedule confirmed at original ticket issuance, not successive
notice-to-notice differences.
6.2 Your choice
Option What is included
Replacement travel One rebooking on this airline to the same destination in the same fare type, within 7
calendar days before or after the original departure date, inclusive, subject to availability. No
change fee or fare difference.
Refund before travel starts For a wholly unused affected itinerary, refund its full fare, unused government taxes and all
unused purchased extras to the original payment method. No cancellation fee, including
Economy Basic.
Refund after travel starts Manual review of the unflown portion and unused extras. The right to refund the unused
affected portion remains; the amount and allocation require review. No refund is promised
for flown segments.
You may choose a refund instead of a credit. A credit is never required as the only remedy. If no suitable
replacement is available, the refund option remains. Choosing and completing a refund ends rebooking eligibility
for the refunded ticket; the same value cannot be refunded twice.
6.3 Request period and later changes
Submit the choice within 30 elapsed days after the disruption notice timestamp, including exactly 30 days. After
that period, eligibility requires manual review rather than automatic approval or rejection. If you accepted
replacement travel and later change your mind for personal reasons, normal voluntary rules apply to the
replacement ticket. A new qualifying disruption creates a new choice.
Keep the disruption notice and identify affected passengers and segments. A pending request does not itself
confirm replacement seats. Hotel, meal and ground-transport compensation are not specified in this publication.
Bluehaven Airways (BHA) | v3.0 | Passenger Policies 4 / 6

7. Cabin and checked baggage
Each passenger has one free personal item up to 40 x 30 x 15 cm and 3 kg. The cabin allowance below is
additional to that personal item. All dimensions include handles and wheels; weights and dimension limits are
inclusive. Allowances are per passenger on each segment and cannot be pooled between travelers.
Fare Cabin bag allowance Checked allowance
Economy Basic No cabin bag No checked bag
Economy Standard 1 cabin bag, 7 kg No checked bag
Economy Flex 1 cabin bag, 10 kg 1 bag, 20 kg
Each permitted cabin bag must be no larger than 55 x 35 x 25 cm. Each checked bag must have length + width
+ height no greater than 158 cm. A bag must satisfy both its weight and size limit. Allowances do not combine
into one heavier bag.
7.1 Purchased baggage
Economy Basic may purchase one cabin bag up to 7 kg for USD 25 per passenger per segment, with the same
cabin dimensions above. Standard and Flex cannot purchase a second cabin bag. These prices are the same
online and at the airport.
One additional checked bag may be purchased for USD 40 per passenger per segment, whether purchased
online or at the airport. Its weight limit is 20 kg and its size limit is 158 cm in summed dimensions. This
purchased-bag limit applies even when a free bag has a different weight limit. No more than one additional
checked bag is covered by this price.
7.2 Items requiring advance review
Overweight, oversized or further additional bags require a service-desk quote and acceptance review; no fixed
charge or acceptance guarantee is provided here. Do not assume that paying an additional-bag fee makes an
overweight bag acceptable. Dangerous goods and special-equipment handling are outside this publication.
7.3 Segment-specific allowance
For a multi-segment journey, assess the allowance and any purchased bag charge on each segment. A
baggage purchase covers only the passenger and segments shown on its receipt. A two-segment trip therefore
incurs two charges for one additional bag carried on both segments.
Example: a Standard traveler taking two segments with one 18 kg checked bag pays 2 x USD 40 = USD 80.
The included cabin bag does not create a free checked allowance.

8. Booking ownership and requests
The named adult traveler may request service for their own ticket after identity and booking details are verified. A
booking reference, shared surname, or possession of payment details alone is not authority. A payer or lead
booker may not change, cancel or view another adult traveler's private ticket information without that traveler's
explicit authorization and identity verification.
A representative must supply the traveler's written authorization naming the representative, booking reference
and permitted action, and complete service-desk verification of both identities. A parent or guardian requesting
service for a minor must provide evidence of guardianship for manual verification. Never send full payment-card
details or identity documents through an unverified channel.
8.1 How to submit a request
For direct bookings, use the fictional service portal https://service.bluehaven-airways.example or email
care@bluehaven-airways.example to begin verification. These are fictional contact details and are not live
services. For agency-issued tickets, contact the issuing agency; this airline's service desk can review disruption
assistance but agency refunds are routed through the issuing agency to the original payment method.
Provide booking reference, traveler names, requested action, affected segments, original issuance timestamp
and any disruption notice. The service desk verifies authority, identifies the applicable rule and provides a quote
or review outcome. Confirm the quoted change or cancellation before execution. A quote alone does not alter a
booking. A complete authorized request includes the required facts, verified authority and acceptance of any
quoted charge; its receipt time determines the policy window.
9. Exceptions requiring manual review
A serious medical event preventing travel may be submitted with dated supporting evidence. Request a secure
submission route before supplying medical records. Approval, waived fees, cash refunds and credit are not
guaranteed. Partly used itinerary refunds, selected-segment cancellations, mixed-fare tickets, disputed
ownership and guardianship also require review. For qualifying disruptions, Section 6 preserves the
unused-portion refund entitlement while the amount is reviewed.
Appendix A. Economy Standard change-fee update
Original ticket issuance (UTC) Early-window change fee
Previous rule: before 2026-07-01 00:00:00 USD 85 per passenger per changed segment
Current rule: at or after 2026-07-01 00:00:00 USD 55 per passenger per changed segment
The late-window prohibition is unchanged. Positive fare differences still apply. The original issuance timestamp
survives reissue. This appendix restates Section 2.1 and changes no other fee or eligibility rule.
10. Topics not covered
Lounge access, pet transport, loyalty benefits and unaccompanied-minor travel services are not documented
here. Contact the service desk for the applicable information; absence of a rule is neither permission nor a
prohibition.
Bluehaven Airways (BHA) | v3.0 | Passenger Policies 6 / 6

2.3 Travel already started
After travel starts, changes to remaining unflown segments follow this table using each segment departure time,
provided no no-show has occurred. A missed segment takes priority over these rules. Voluntary refunds of partly
used tickets are handled only under Section 9.
Example: one Economy Standard traveler changes one domestic and one international segment, both 30 hours
before departure. Fees are USD 20 + USD 65 = USD 85. Positive fare differences and any tax adjustment are
additional.

3. Voluntary cancellation and refunds
This section applies when you choose not to travel and Section 6 does not apply. The table covers cancellation
of the entire wholly unused itinerary for each selected passenger. Cancellation fees are per passenger, per
itinerary, not per segment or per booking.
Fare Early: at least 24 hours Late: more than 0, less than 24 hours
Economy Basic No fare refund or credit No fare refund or credit
Economy Standard Domestic credit less USD 25; international No fare refund or credit
no fare refund or credit
Economy Flex Domestic original payment, USD 0 fee; Domestic original payment less USD 20;
international original payment less USD 50 international credit less USD 75
3.1 Amount and payment destination
Fare means the ticket amount excluding separately itemized government taxes and optional services. Where the
table allows a refund or credit, subtract the stated fee from the eligible fare; the result cannot be below USD 0.
No additional balance is collected when the fee exceeds the fare. Unused government taxes are returned to the
original payment method on request for every fare, including non-refundable fares and no-shows.
An original-payment refund returns to the payment instrument used for the original purchase. Paying for another
traveler does not make the fare transferable. A travel credit is issued in the named passenger's name, cannot be
transferred or exchanged for cash, and may be used only with this airline. Unused credit remains available until
expiry.
3.2 Credit validity and optional services
A credit expires exactly 365 elapsed days after issue. It must be redeemed before that instant; redemption at the
expiry instant is not permitted. The new travel must also begin before that expiry instant. There is no extension
under the standard policy.
Purchased baggage and seat extras are non-refundable for a voluntary cancellation. On an eligible date/time
change, unused extras transfer to the same passenger and route without a transfer fee, subject to availability;
unavailable services require manual review. No automatic cash refund is promised for unavailable extras.
4. Cancellation scope
One traveler may cancel their own whole ticket without cancelling other travelers in the booking, after authority is
verified. A request to cancel selected segments only, or any refund after a segment has been flown, requires
Section 9 review; do not apply the whole-ticket table to an assumed remaining balance.
5. No-shows
A traveler is a no-show if no complete authorized change/cancellation request was received before departure
and the traveler does not take that flight. At exactly departure time, a new voluntary request is too late and
receives no-show treatment. All remaining segments are suspended pending service-desk contact; there is no
automatic reinstatement. The remaining fare has no standard refund or credit, including Flex. Unused
government taxes remain refundable. A qualifying airline disruption under Section 6 takes precedence; medical
circumstances may be reviewed under Section 9.

6. Airline-initiated disruptions
These protections apply when the airline cancels a segment or makes a qualifying schedule change. They
override the voluntary fare restrictions, change fees and no-show loss of value in Sections 2, 3 and 5 for the
affected journey. A passenger choosing to cancel for personal reasons without a qualifying event remains
subject to the voluntary rules.
6.1 Qualifying events
A cancellation by Suntrail Air qualifies for all fare types. A schedule change qualifies when the absolute
difference between the original and revised scheduled departure time of a segment is 120 minutes or more,
including exactly 120 minutes, whether moved earlier or later. Smaller changes do not qualify under this
document. Compare the latest notice with the schedule confirmed at original ticket issuance, not successive
notice-to-notice differences.
6.2 Your choice
Option What is included
Replacement travel One rebooking on this airline to the same destination in the same fare type, within 7
calendar days before or after the original departure date, inclusive, subject to availability. No
change fee or fare difference.
Refund before travel starts For a wholly unused affected itinerary, refund its full fare, unused government taxes and all
unused purchased extras to the original payment method. No cancellation fee, including
Economy Basic.
Refund after travel starts Manual review of the unflown portion and unused extras. The right to refund the unused
affected portion remains; the amount and allocation require review. No refund is promised
for flown segments.
You may choose a refund instead of a credit. A credit is never required as the only remedy. If no suitable
replacement is available, the refund option remains. Choosing and completing a refund ends rebooking eligibility
for the refunded ticket; the same value cannot be refunded twice.
6.3 Request period and later changes
Submit the choice within 30 elapsed days after the disruption notice timestamp, including exactly 30 days. After
that period, eligibility requires manual review rather than automatic approval or rejection. If you accepted
replacement travel and later change your mind for personal reasons, normal voluntary rules apply to the
replacement ticket. A new qualifying disruption creates a new choice.
Keep the disruption notice and identify affected passengers and segments. A pending request does not itself
confirm replacement seats. Hotel, meal and ground-transport compensation are not specified in this publication.

7. Cabin and checked baggage
Each passenger has one free personal item up to 40 x 30 x 15 cm and 3 kg. The cabin allowance below is
additional to that personal item. All dimensions include handles and wheels; weights and dimension limits are
inclusive. Allowances are per passenger on each segment and cannot be pooled between travelers.
Fare Cabin bag allowance Checked allowance
Economy Basic 1 cabin bag, 7 kg Domestic: none; international: 1 bag, 20 kg
Economy Standard 1 cabin bag, 10 kg Domestic: 1 bag, 20 kg; international: 1 bag,
23 kg
Economy Flex 1 cabin bag, 12 kg Domestic: 2 bags, 20 kg each; international:
2 bags, 23 kg each
Each permitted cabin bag must be no larger than 55 x 35 x 25 cm. Each checked bag must have length + width
+ height no greater than 158 cm. A bag must satisfy both its weight and size limit. Allowances do not combine
into one heavier bag.
7.1 Purchased baggage
A second cabin bag cannot be purchased under this policy. Items beyond the cabin allowance must meet the
checked-baggage rules or be reviewed before acceptance.
One additional checked bag may be purchased for USD 50 per passenger per segment, whether purchased
online or at the airport. Its weight limit is 23 kg and its size limit is 158 cm in summed dimensions. This
purchased-bag limit applies even when a free bag has a different weight limit. No more than one additional
checked bag is covered by this price.
7.2 Items requiring advance review
Overweight, oversized or further additional bags require a service-desk quote and acceptance review; no fixed
charge or acceptance guarantee is provided here. Do not assume that paying an additional-bag fee makes an
overweight bag acceptable. Dangerous goods and special-equipment handling are outside this publication.
7.3 Segment-specific allowance
For a multi-segment journey, assess the allowance and any purchased bag charge on each segment. A
baggage purchase covers only the passenger and segments shown on its receipt. A two-segment trip therefore
incurs two charges for one additional bag carried on both segments.
Example: Economy Basic includes no checked bag on an Aster domestic segment and one 20 kg checked bag
on an international segment. Carrying a 19 kg bag on both requires a USD 50 purchase on the domestic
segment only; the international segment includes it.

8. Booking ownership and requests
The named adult traveler may request service for their own ticket after identity and booking details are verified. A
booking reference, shared surname, or possession of payment details alone is not authority. A payer or lead
booker may not change, cancel or view another adult traveler's private ticket information without that traveler's
explicit authorization and identity verification.
A representative must supply the traveler's written authorization naming the representative, booking reference
and permitted action, and complete service-desk verification of both identities. A parent or guardian requesting
service for a minor must provide evidence of guardianship for manual verification. Never send full payment-card
details or identity documents through an unverified channel.
8.1 How to submit a request
For direct bookings, use the fictional service portal https://service.suntrail-air.example or email
care@suntrail-air.example to begin verification. These are fictional contact details and are not live services. For
agency-issued tickets, contact the issuing agency; this airline's service desk can review disruption assistance
but agency refunds are routed through the issuing agency to the original payment method.
Provide booking reference, traveler names, requested action, affected segments, original issuance timestamp
and any disruption notice. The service desk verifies authority, identifies the applicable rule and provides a quote
or review outcome. Confirm the quoted change or cancellation before execution. A quote alone does not alter a
booking. A complete authorized request includes the required facts, verified authority and acceptance of any
quoted charge; its receipt time determines the policy window.
9. Exceptions requiring manual review
A serious medical event preventing travel may be submitted with dated supporting evidence. Request a secure
submission route before supplying medical records. Approval, waived fees, cash refunds and credit are not
guaranteed. Partly used itinerary refunds, selected-segment cancellations, mixed-fare tickets, disputed
ownership and guardianship also require review. For qualifying disruptions, Section 6 preserves the
unused-portion refund entitlement while the amount is reviewed.
9.1 Supporting information and review outcome
Keep receipts and identify flown and unused segments when requesting a partial refund. The service desk
confirms what evidence is needed. A review request is not an approval, and the standard rules remain
applicable unless a specific exception is approved. No fixed review or refund-processing turnaround is promised
here.
10. Topics not covered
Lounge access, pet transport, loyalty benefits and unaccompanied-minor travel services are not documented
here. Contact the service desk for the applicable information; absence of a rule is neither permission nor a
prohibition.
